Risk / thesis breaker

The offer transfers treasury stock and does not increase issued shares; the latest Q3 shows growth/profit and improving capital ratio. Still, FY2027 operating-profit forecast rises 76.2% and there is no prior-year Q3 comparison, while the second tranche’s EPS effect is omitted from the presented forecast. Strong revenue/stock mix and low reported churn are promising, but construction contributes 68.8% of sales, while FY2027/9 assumes 20.3% revenue growth and a large OP-margin increase to 29.0%. AITURBO remains early-stage (13 customers, ¥15.77m ARR); growth-record YAU is forecast flat in FY2027; the company itself flags migration/adoption, churn, construction concentration, cyclical demand, AI/competition, cybersecurity and hiring risks. TAM estimates are explicitly company-defined potential maxima, not objective addressable market. Control concentration is removed and public float likely rises, which may improve liquidity/governance; company reports no operating impact. However, insider sale removes the former CEO’s ownership and is a potential overhang/control transition, with no explanation here of new controlling holders or lock-up details.
